Both are a suspension of breath beyond the phases of inhalation and exhalation; the Yoga Sūtra's 'fourth' is defined by going beyond the outer and inner spheres, the haṭha kevala by the absence of inhalation and exhalation. The texts do not themselves identify them.
The Vivekamārtaṇḍa names the seal nabhomudrā where the Haṭhapradīpikā has khecarī; the Gheraṇḍa describes nabhomudrā as a separate, simpler practice (tongue turned up, breath held, anywhere).
The Gheraṇḍa's yoni mudrā includes the closing of the six openings that is elsewhere the whole of ṣaṇmukhī; the Śivasaṃhitā's yoni mudrā is a perineal contraction.
Śāṇḍilya Up. 1.31 defines vaiṣṇavī mudrā in the very terms by which HYP 4.36 defines śāmbhavī (inner target, outward unblinking gaze).
Both empty the stomach upward; gajakaraṇī does it by raising apāna to the throat, vamana-dhauti after drinking water.
Both cleanse the anus with the finger; the Haṭharatnāvalī names its act cakrī.
Brahmānanda explains niyamāgraha (HYP 1.15) as cold bathing at dawn, eating at night, eating only fruit — the same mortifications the Gorakṣa verse (HYP 1.61) forbids.
Both divide breath-control by the presence or absence of a support; the Viṣṇu Purāṇa's support is the Lord's form, the Gheraṇḍa's the seed-syllables with the three gods.
Defined in identical terms (antarlakṣya, bahirdṛṣṭi, nimeṣonmeṣa-varjitā).
Preliminaries of prāṇāyāma, the fifth of the Gheraṇḍa's seven means.
